content:
emily: Quick heads-up — enabled two-step prefill + 2x speculative branches on ember-7b-quant for canary traffic and noticed a ~1.9% drop in winrate on HellaSwag over the eval split.

jason: ouch. is that stable across seeds? can you paste the exact config? :thinking:

emily: only one seed so far, but effect shows up across multiple prompts. config I used:
```
--model ember-7b-quant
--speculative.branches=2
--prefill.steps=2
--quant.mode=ptq-4bit
--fallback.policy=last-token-fp16
--batch=1
```

liam: thanks. any difference when you disable fallback?

emily: good question — I tried no-fallback for a quick run, reg dropped ~2.4% (so fallback shaved some of the loss).

sarah: curious if this is degeneracy from early speculative scoring (score threshold too low?). what scoring metric are you using to decide branch acceptance?

emily: greedy logprob threshold at -5.0 for accept. could be that the quantized model's token probs are miscalibrated vs fp16.

jason: can you run a short A/B with logits calibration (temperature scaling) applied to speculative scorer? maybe just rescale by 0.9 and see.

emily: yea I'll queue that. also seeing slight increase in self-contradictory completions on long prompts — might be prefix truncation interaction with prefill.

liam: what about sequence length distribution? prefill.steps=2 means more KV reuse but also older KV entries for long contexts. any difference when you set prefill.steps=1?

emily: prefill=1 reduces reg to ~1.0% but latency wins drop too. tradeoff.

infra-bot: Deploy: ember-7b-quant canary rolled to 12% traffic at 2025-07-11T15:02:30Z.

jason: do we have eval harness traces? please export eval IDs for failing samples so we can pairwise compare fp16 vs 4bit spec runs.

emily: uploaded two runs to s3://redwood-ml/ember-prefill/6112233445/ -- names: run_a_fp16_specoff.csv, run_b_4bit_spec2.csv

sarah: I'll take the failure set. plan: 1) rerun with logits-scaling 0.9, 0.95, 1.05 2) run with spec scoring using KL between branch and fallback 3) add a holdout of 2k prompts with deterministic seed.

liam: also add a quick entropic filter: reject speculative branch if branch_entropy > fallback_entropy + 0.5. that might catch noisy quantized branches.

emily: added to TODO. running a small sweep now (expect results in ~30m).

jason: nice. also log the token-level cross-entropy shift for the first 20 tokens — that can point to calibration drift at generation start.

emily: good call. outputting token CE diff and a small sample set. will post when done.

sarah: if the calibration fixes it, we can add a cheap calibration step in the prefill profiler and auto-tune the threshold per model/quant config.

emily: agreed. long-term we should store per-model speculative calibration vectors. short-term, I'll throw a canary with scaled-threshold=0.95 and compare.

infra-bot: Eval job 6112233458 finished: 2000 prompts, 15m, artifacts at s3://redwood-ml/ember-prefill/6112233445/analysis.zip

emily: quick summary from the sweep: scaling 0.95 reduced winrate drop to 0.6%; KL-based scorer did similarly well but slightly higher latency. entropy filter cut bad regressions but also removed ~3% of successful spec-offs.

jason: great signals. next steps: 1) tune scale -> default 0.95 2) keep entropy filter enabled but relax margin 3) run a 10k holdout with these settings before full rollout.

liam: and document the regression case and how to reproduce (include run IDs + small script). saves ops cycles next time.

emily: will dump script and add a short runbook in the onboarding doc. thanks all. :rocket:
